Intrepid Travel launches 10‑day Antarctic Peninsula Pure Expedition aboard the Ocean Victory

Overview

Intrepid Travel, in partnership with Polar Latitudes, is promoting a 10‑day expedition that sails the Antarctic Peninsula and the South Shetland Islands. The trip is marketed under the name “Antarctic Peninsula: The Pure Expedition (Ocean Victory)” and is positioned as a high‑end, wildlife‑focused journey that combines ship‑board comfort with daily Zodiac and kayak excursions.

Confirmed Details

  • Operator: Intrepid Travel (Polar Latitudes as the polar partner)
  • Ship: *Ocean Victory* – a purpose‑built polar vessel with Ice Class 1A and Polar Class 6 certifications.
  • Duration: 10 days (including two days crossing the Drake Passage).
  • Destination region: Antarctic Peninsula and the South Shetland Islands, departing from Ushuaia, Argentina.
  • Physical rating: Listed as a moderate‑to‑high exertion trip; participants need reasonable fitness for wet‑landings, Zodiac work and occasional steep terrain.

Reported Highlights (as described by Intrepid Travel)

  • Wildlife encounters – colonies of chinstrap and gentoo penguins, elephant and fur seals, humpback whales, and seabirds such as Antarctic terns and wandering albatrosses.
  • Scientific sites – visits to active research bases and historic landing locations, with on‑board talks from the expedition team.
  • Citizen‑Science program – passengers can contribute data on Antarctic ecosystems, supporting climate‑change research.
  • Optional night‑camping – a paid add‑on that lets travelers sleep under the polar sky.
  • On‑board amenities – wellness centre (spa, gym), two panoramic Jacuzzis, cabins (most with private balconies), and observation decks with hydraulic platforms for low‑level water views.

Inclusions & Exclusions (as far as the source indicates)

  • Included:
  • Transfer from Ushuaia airport to the port (only if arrival is on Day 1).
  • Accommodation on *Ocean Victory* for the full itinerary.
  • Daily Zodiac excursions (approximately two per day, weather‑dependent).
  • Participation in the Citizen‑Science program.
  • Access to ship facilities (spa, gym, Jacuzzis, observation decks).
  • Not confirmed / likely excluded:
  • International flights to/from Ushuaia (the page notes they must be booked separately).
  • Personal gear such as waterproof boots and jackets (these are loaned, but the cost is not specified).
  • Optional activities (kayaking, camping, photography program) which require separate pre‑booking and payment.

How to Verify and Book

  1. Visit the official product page – the URL `https://www.intrepidtravel.com/uk/antarctica/antarctic-peninsula-pure-expedition-ocean-victory-178871` contains the most up‑to‑date itinerary, pricing, and terms.
  2. Contact an Intrepid sales agent – the page advises speaking with a booking agent for flight quotes, optional activities, and visa assistance.
  3. Review Polar Latitudes’ booking conditions – the deposit and payment schedule are outlined under the partner’s “booking conditions” section on Intrepid’s site.
  4. Check for updates – because Antarctic itineraries can change due to weather or ice conditions, travelers should confirm the final sailing dates and any itinerary adjustments before final payment.

Implications for Travelers

  • Adventure vs. comfort – The expedition blends rigorous fieldwork (Zodiacs, kayaking, possible camping) with upscale ship amenities, appealing to travelers who want both physical activity and luxury.
  • Environmental responsibility – Participation in citizen‑science projects and Intrepid’s climate‑commitment statements suggest a focus on sustainable tourism, though the exact carbon footprint of the voyage is still being calculated.
  • Health considerations – The ship carries a doctor and provides over‑the‑counter seasickness medication; however, rough seas on the Drake Passage can cause motion sickness for some passengers.
  • Flexibility required – The itinerary notes that weather may alter landings or Zodiac schedules, so travelers should be prepared for last‑minute changes.

Bottom line: Intrepid Travel’s new Antarctic Peninsula Pure Expedition offers a well‑structured, 10‑day polar adventure aboard a modern ice‑strengthened vessel. Prospective guests should verify pricing, exact sailing windows, and any additional costs directly through Intrepid’s website or a sales representative before committing.
